Container.Name: backup-manager
Container.Overview:
Backup Manager pulls backup artifacts off a remote SFTP source on a schedule, verifies them, retains them under a configurable policy, and keeps a durable catalog of everything it holds.
This is the engine container: the API, the scheduler and local authentication. It deliberately publishes no port. Install backup-manager-ui alongside it for the web interface.
Before installing: run `docker network create backup-manager`, create the appdata path and the backup-manager directory inside your backups share, own them by the uid/gid below, and write config.yaml, the SSH key and the pinned known_hosts. The engine validates its config before it opens a listener, so a missing config file stops it starting.
This container does not trust X-Forwarded-For or X-Forwarded-Proto, so its login, enrollment and password rate limiters count every request against the Web UI container's address: one shared bucket rather than one per client. That is deliberate. The network these two containers share is created by hand and lives on the host, so anything attached to it later becomes a direct peer of this container and could otherwise forge those headers to defeat the limiter. The compose profiles use a project-scoped network and can trust the headers; this profile is the one place that guarantee is weaker.
Container.Requires: Run `docker network create backup-manager` before installing, and install the companion backup-manager-ui template for the web interface.

Config.Name: Application state
Config.Description: Holds the SQLite catalog and the local-authentication administrator record. Must exist and be owned by the uid/gid in ExtraParams before first start.

Config.Name: Backup root
Config.Description: Where retained artifacts land: a directory of this app's own inside a real user share, never a directory inside appdata and never the share itself. Keeping it a dedicated child means installing, reinstalling and removing this app only ever touches paths it created, even when the share already holds data from something else. No key material or authentication state may ever live inside the backup root.

Config.Name: Configuration directory
Config.Description: A WRITABLE DIRECTORY the app owns, with config.yaml inside it (issue #196). Not a read-only file: adding a backup set, saving settings and first-run setup all replace config.yaml through a temp file created in this directory, and the engine's ssh_keys/ and known_hosts.d/ stores are siblings of it. It may be empty on a fresh install. Must exist and be owned by the uid/gid in ExtraParams before first start. UPGRADING FROM AN EARLIER TEMPLATE: a changed Target does not retire a mapping already in your own template copy, so delete the old "Configuration file" path mapping (Target /etc/backup-manager/config.yaml) by hand. Leaving both mounts in place bind-mounts config.yaml over this directory and the engine stops with a message naming issue #196.

Config.Name: SFTP private key
Config.Description: Mounted read-only. Keep it at mode 0600 on the host. It is never baked into the image.

Config.Name: Pinned known_hosts
Config.Description: Mounted read-only. Verify the remote's host-key fingerprint out of band before trusting this file.

Config.Name: TMPDIR
Config.Description: Go's temp directory. The rootfs is read-only, so this has to point at the tmpfs in ExtraParams.

Config.Name: Listen address
Config.Description: The engine's own listen address inside the container. Never published to the LAN.

Config.Name: Public base URL
Config.Description: What the Web UI container's published port looks like from outside this server. The engine prints its one-time enrollment link against this, because its own listen address is never reachable. Set your server's real hostname and the port you gave backup-manager-ui.
